architecture.callerIngressLaw: Projected caller input is neither Agent-owned durable WorkingSet selection nor arbitrary overlay. After a needs_input pause, exact plain caller user messages supplied on resume form caller-owned interaction cognition until the next needs_input Snapshot establishes a new interaction boundary.
architecture.authorityPartition: The effective model view is partitioned into Agent-selected durable WorkingSet cognition, caller-owned interaction ingress, attempt-local Provider/Tool cognition, and Harness-owned per-turn execution control. Each layer has a different owner and lifetime.
architecture.durableBoundary: The latest needs_input Snapshot state is the caller-interaction boundary. Continuity mechanically derives the current caller ingress as the initial consecutive exact plain user-message suffix after that Snapshot state. No new conversation table or caller-message database is introduced.
architecture.chronologyLaw: Journal sequence orders current-attempt Provider Tool exchanges around the needs_input pause. Recovery therefore reconstructs pre-caller Tool exchanges, then caller ingress, then post-caller Tool exchanges without guessing transcript chronology.
architecture.workingSetLaw: Caller ingress does not create a HarnessWorkingViewSource or WorkingSet pin and does not mutate Agent-owned durable selection. It survives WorkingSet transitions during the same caller interaction while predecessor attempt-local Tool exchanges still expire at the WorkingSet boundary.
architecture.pauseConsumptionLaw: The next needs_input Snapshot consumes the current caller interaction. A later resume derives only caller messages after that newer Snapshot, so earlier caller ingress is not accumulated as permanent memory.
architecture.admissionLaw: Before physical Provider dispatch, Continuity recomputes the exact permitted WorkingView suffix from Snapshot/RunState caller evidence plus Provider/Tool Journal evidence. A bridge-local fabricated caller message cannot become Provider cognition authority.
architecture.shapeLaw: Projected resume caller ingress accepts only exact plain messages with role=user and string content. Caller-supplied system, assistant, Tool-shaped or structurally enriched messages fail before Provider dispatch. Non-projected legacy resume behavior is unchanged.
architecture.progressLaw: A newly admitted caller ingress may reset soft observation/no-progress counters because the new caller bytes now actually enter the effective model view. It does not revive hard Tool-call budget.
architecture.privacyLaw: Caller ingress is model content rather than a Tool channel. It requires model-content authority for exact durable/cross-process use but does not by itself require Tool-content authority. If the same effective transcript also contains Tool exchanges, those exchanges retain their stricter Tool-content requirement.
architecture.schemaChange: No SQLite schema, Protocol codec, generic Conversation Store, Memory subsystem, caller-message table or recommended public API was added.

behavior.visibleResume: A Run first exhausted a one-turn soft observation allowance and paused needs_input. A plain caller reply was then resumed through the Snapshot-bound projected path. The next Provider request contained the exact caller message after the pre-pause Tool exchange, the soft gate reopened because model-visible cognition actually changed, and no additional Runtime dispatch occurred merely from admitting the caller input.
behavior.workingSetTransition: A caller reply followed by an Agent WorkingSet transition from [A] to [A,B] remained visible in both the transition-authoring Provider view and the successor Provider view. The transition changed only Agent durable selection; caller interaction cognition remained until the next needs_input boundary.
behavior.pauseConsumption: needs_input -> OLD caller reply -> needs_input -> NEW caller reply produced a later Provider view containing NEW but not OLD. The second needs_input Snapshot became the new interaction boundary rather than turning caller replies into unbounded transcript memory.
behavior.toolProcessLoss: After needs_input, a caller reply was followed by a Provider-authored Runtime Tool call. The Tool observation became durable and the process was then lost. A fresh process reconstructed base WorkingView + caller reply + assistant Tool call + Tool Observation in that exact order; the completed Tool effect was not redispatched.
behavior.providerResponseLoss: After needs_input and caller reply, the Provider completed durably and the bridge response was lost. A fresh process resumed from the original needs_input Snapshot without re-supplying the caller reply, reconstructed caller cognition from durable Provider/RunState continuity, replayed the exact Provider result with zero Provider redispatch, and preserved a healthy Continuity Doctor.
behavior.forgeryAttack: A malicious Runtime bridge returned the legitimate caller ingress plus an invented user message. The Loop projected the bridge result, but Continuity recomputed the expected suffix from durable Snapshot/RunState authority and rejected the mismatch before the Scripted Provider adapter was invoked.
behavior.roleAttack: A projected resume carrying a system-role message was rejected as invalid caller cognition ingress before any Provider invocation. The projected caller surface therefore does not become a generic arbitrary-message overlay.
behavior.modelOnlyPrivacy: A deterministic no-Tool Run with allow_model_content=true and allow_tool_content=false paused needs_input, resumed with an exact caller user message, and projected base source + caller message successfully. This proves caller ingress does not borrow Tool-content authority.
behavior.realDeepSeek: A live deepseek-v4-flash no-Tool Run received a selected task source that explicitly lacked the launch code. Turn 1 returned needs_input and the captured Provider wire did not contain BLUE-17. The Run resumed with the caller message 'the current launch code is BLUE-17'. Turn 2's captured Provider wire contained the task source followed by that exact caller message; DeepSeek returned candidate_completed with summary stating the authoritative current launch code is BLUE-17. Continuity Doctor remained healthy.

conclusion: P-C1.10 closes the projected caller-input gap without weakening Agent WorkingSet ownership or reopening arbitrary message overlays. The latest needs_input Snapshot acts as a durable interaction boundary; plain caller user messages after that boundary become a separate caller-owned cognition layer, are ordered with attempt-local Tool exchanges by Journal sequence, remain visible across Agent WorkingSet transitions, and expire at the next needs_input pause. Continuity revalidates the effective suffix from durable authority before Provider dispatch and can reconstruct it after Tool process loss or Provider response loss without caller resend. Real deepseek-v4-flash independently demonstrated the intended interaction: needs_input with no code, then candidate_completed after BLUE-17 entered through the caller ingress. No Memory system, Conversation Store, new persistence schema or public cognition API was required.
knownLimits: Caller-owned means input supplied by the current Harness caller at the resume boundary. P-C1.10 does not authenticate a human identity, establish multi-user authorship or prove that caller-provided facts are true in the external world.

Projected caller ingress is currently defined only after a durable needs_input Snapshot and only for exact plain user messages with string content. Structured attachments, multimodal input, system instructions, assistant messages and Tool-shaped caller payloads are not admitted by this surface.

Caller ingress is interaction-scoped, not durable memory. It intentionally expires when the next needs_input Snapshot starts a new caller interaction unless the Agent separately selects/materializes appropriate durable cognition through existing domain/WorkingSet mechanisms.
Exact cross-process caller-ingress reconstruction requires retained model content. Metadata-only continuity may preserve digests/fences but cannot recreate omitted caller bytes.

When Tool exchanges coexist with caller ingress, exact reconstruction still requires Tool-content authority for the Tool portions even though the caller messages themselves require only model-content authority.

P-C1.10 proves recovery after caller bytes cross an existing durable RunState/Provider/Tool Snapshot boundary. It does not claim recovery if a process disappears before newly supplied caller bytes have been durably bound anywhere.

The current chronology rule uses Journal event ordering plus the latest needs_input Snapshot. It does not create a general-purpose editable conversation log or arbitrary transcript-reordering facility.

The Harness does not semantically judge whether caller input is relevant, sufficient or safe to promote into durable WorkingSet cognition. The Agent/domain remains responsible for any later selection or materialization decision.
The one live deepseek-v4-flash probe demonstrates capability usability for a simple needs_input -> caller reply -> completion path, not general model competence across complex interactive tasks.
No Runtime, World, Finance or Host repository was changed.
